question: At 25°C, the barrier potential for germanium is approximately equal to:
solution:
The correct answer is __0.3 V**(Option 1)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Barrier potential__ is the voltage developed across the depletion region of a semiconductor diode.
 
• At 25°C, the barrier potential for germanium is approximately 0.3 V.
 
• Barrier potential depends on factors such as temperature, material type, and doping levels.
 
• For silicon, the barrier potential is typically 0.7 V, which is higher than that of germanium.
 
• Germanium diodes are used in low voltage and high-speed applications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Silicon vs Germanium:**
 
 
• Silicon has a higher barrier potential (0.7 V) compared to germanium (0.3 V).
 
• Germanium has a lower bandgap, making it more suitable for low-voltage applications.
 
 
 
• **Depletion Region:**
 
 
• The depletion region is the area near the p-n junction where charge carriers are depleted.
 
• It acts as a barrier to the flow of charge carriers, resulting in the barrier potential.
 
 
 
• **Temperature Dependence:**
 
 
• The barrier potential decreases with an increase in temperature.
 
• This is due to increased thermal energy overcoming the potential barrier.
